MISCHIEF WEB SDK · DEVELOPER PREVIEW 0.1

A little more human.
Inside your app.

Embed the emoji mixer in your app-owned composer. Receive PNG or GIF bytes, suggested meaning, ingredient names, and accessible alternative text.

Open the composer demo ↗ · Open Mischief

Web integration

Self-host the complete kit on your app's origin. Import the SDK and mount it where your sticker picker belongs.

import { mountMischief } from './mischief/brand-sdk.mjs';

const picker = mountMischief(document.querySelector('#picker'), {
  brand: 'Your brand',
  accent: '#b3d8ff',
  onSelect(sticker) {
    // Your app owns insertion, attachment upload, and sending.
    // sticker.blob: PNG or GIF
    // sticker.alt: accessible description
    // sticker.meaning: title, description, intent, traits, confidence
    // sticker.ingredients: emoji, name, category, meaning
    // sticker.animated, width, height, mimeType
    addAttachmentToDraft(sticker.blob, sticker.alt);
  }
});

// When your composer closes:
picker.destroy();

addAttachmentToDraft is the host app's function, not part of this SDK. See the working demo for DOM insertion. The component does not read messages, send messages, or collect analytics. Meaning is returned as metadata and accessible alt text; the mixer shows no caption on its result.

Meaning travels with the sticker

Authored rules suggest a reading. The mixer stays visual: no explanatory caption appears with the result. Mixed emotions are acknowledged. All ingredients remain in the semantic metadata, even when the title summarizes the dominant emotion.

The image itself does not contain a caption. Use the alt text for accessibility and keep meaning metadata for app-owned discovery or classification. These rules do not guarantee a universal interpretation or infer the user's actual feelings.

Platform boundaries

  • App-owned keyboards and composers: the builder can place this component within its own UI and handle returned attachments.
  • Android system keyboard: a separate native IME must use Commit Content with the MIME types accepted by the receiving app. No IME or APK is included.
  • iPhone/iPad: a separate signed keyboard or messaging extension is required. Secure fields and some apps exclude custom keyboards. No iOS extension is included.
  • Windows: build an app-owned picker or separate companion picker. This package does not extend the Windows emoji panel.

Deployment and updates

The current hosted app is a private preview. Do not use it as a production dependency for third-party customers. Self-host the files, allow the iframe in your Content Security Policy, and serve modules with JavaScript MIME types. Keep the SDK and mixer on the same release. For cached installed apps, change the service worker cache version with each release; updates apply after old tabs close.

Before a commercial release

This is a developer preview, not a tested native SDK. Validate iframe policy, accessibility, rendering, export, mobile behavior, and attachment insertion in each host. The kit includes 3,953 Unicode 17.0 emoji sequences and components. Emoji artwork currently uses device fonts, may vary across platforms, and newer sequences may not render on older systems. A consistent commercial art library and its usage rights need to be selected before branded distribution.

Brand name and accent configuration are implemented. Exclusive asset packs, tenant management, billing, contractual exclusivity, native packages, AI generation, and service-level commitments are not included.

Platform references: Android image keyboard support, Apple keyboard limitations, Windows input methods.
